paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. God's message does not need Paul free to move. Paul comes to Rome in a chain, and Luke ends the book with this: "Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ." (Acts 28:31) The man is bound, and the message is NOT. I spent years stuck in a drawer, so believe me, I love hearing that.

Notice who shows up for Paul along the way. The brothers from Rome travel out to meet him, and "When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God." (Acts 28:15) Even Paul needed encouragement, and God sent it through people. Then look at how the people respond to his teaching: some are convinced, others refuse (Acts 28:24). Same message, same teacher, different hearts. That's still how it goes, so don't be shocked when it does.

And Paul keeps the door open anyway. He welcomes "all who come to visit him" (Acts 28:30), and he says, "God's salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!" (Acts 28:28) That means the good news is for people far from where it started, and that includes you. So here's your job, baker: be ready to listen, and keep your door open. The story of Paul in Rome ends here, but the message he preached keeps going out FREE.
